fact: Linear B uses o-pe-ro (and abbreviated o) for amounts owed/shortfalls in deciphered accounting contexts.
diagnostic: A deficit status can be lexically distinguished; list shape alone is not enough.

fact: Ayios Vasileios personnel records use a-pe-o-te, interpreted as absent, with men/personnel context.
diagnostic: In a deciphered comparator, absence has an overt modifier; do not infer Linear A absence solely from one-count sublist structure.

fact: Pylos Ma records distinguish expected assessment, actual delivery (a-pu-do-si), exemptions (o-u-di-do-si), and owed amounts (o-pe-ro).
diagnostic: Direction/polarity comes from lexical/documentary contrasts, not arithmetic template alone.
